title: Thorn and Garden
premise: Oscar Kavanagh has spent her life as the invisible keeper of a sealed gate in the Thornfell mountains, tending a door her family has guarded for generations without ever being told why. When a child arrives speaking a language older than any kingdom, Oscar learns she is heir to more than a gate: she is the last key to Vael, a country erased from maps and memory, and the child is its displaced heir. As smugglers, crown soldiers, and the ghost-wardens of Vael converge on Thornfell before the moon's thirteenth turn, Oscar must choose between her sworn duty to keep the gate shut and the found family forming around the girl. In the end, Oscar opens the gate not as an escape route but as a bridge—restoring Vael as a hidden country alongside our own—and takes her place not as a keeper of doors, but as the first ambassador between two worlds.
about_author: Casper Villalobos is a former cartographer who once mapped mountain passes for a living and now maps imaginary countries instead. They write fantasy about borders, both real and remembered, from a cabin full of obsolete atlases.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Moon Rises
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. On a routine patrol of the smuggler roads, Oscar finds a half-frozen child at the gatehouse door, speaking a tongue no scholar would recognize—yet Oscar's grandmother's lullabies almost match it. The emotional beat is wary tenderness: duty says turn the child away, but something inherited in Oscar's blood says open the door.

chapters.title: What the Gate Remembers
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, with interludes from the child, Wren. Deciphering Wren's language through old family journals, Oscar learns the gate seals the border of Vael, a country unmade by treaty and forgetting—and that her family were its wardens, not its jailers. Crown riders arrive asking questions. The beat is dread mixed with wonder as inheritance becomes burden.

chapters.title: A Country with No Door Out
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Oscar and Captain Ilse Marchand, the soldier hunting Wren. Smugglers Oscar has traded with for years become unlikely allies, sheltering them in the deep roads while ghost-wardens of old Vael test Oscar's right to the key. The climax strikes at the gate itself: Ilse demands it be destroyed, Wren begs it be opened, and Oscar must decide what duty truly means. The beat is sacrifice—Oscar chooses love over obedience.

chapters.title: Thorn and Garden
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, closing with Wren's. The gate opens onto Vael—not restored, but alive beneath its forgetting—and Oscar walks Wren home, then refuses to seal it behind her. The crown, faced with a country that was never legally abolished, negotiates rather than fights. The resolution is quiet: a garden planted on the threshold, two families grafted into one, and Oscar finally visible, standing in her own doorway.
